procedure.description: insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 33249 (insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead) with date of service 2026-02-06. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish an ejection fraction of 35 percent or less after an adequate trial of guideline-directed medical therapy.

criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction of 35 percent or less on echocardiography, nuclear study, or cardiac MRI, measured after at least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy.
New York Heart Association class II or III heart failure symptoms.

At least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy including a beta blocker and an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI, with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist and an SGLT2 inhibitor as tolerated, at maximally tolerated doses.
More than 40 days after any myocardial infarction and more than 90 days after any coronary revascularization.
Expected survival with good functional status of more than one year.

chart.text: Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.5, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.

71 year old woman in cardiology clinic for ischemic cardiomyopathy after her infarction. Reviewed the plan: optimize medications, repeat the echo in 3 months, and decide on a defibrillator then. She understands the device is for sudden death prevention, not symptoms. Her history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 3 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Anterior ST-elevation infarction 10 months ago, drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending at that time. No revascularization since; no residual ischemia on the follow-up stress study. No other life-limiting illness, independent, still working. Expected survival well over a year.
Blood pressure check. 146 over 85 today, 141 over 75 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Transthoracic echocardiogram. Left ventricular ejection fraction 25 percent by biplane Simpson’s, anterior and apical akinesis, mild mitral regurgitation, no thrombus.

Carvedilol 25 twice daily, sacubitril-valsartan 97/103 twice daily, spironolactone 25 daily, empagliflozin 10 daily. All four started after the infarction and titrated to these doses by the second cardiology visit; doses unchanged since.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
A1c came back 6.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Three-month visit. Reviewed the repeat echocardiogram with her. Discussed primary prevention defibrillator, risks of implant, what a shock feels like, driving rules. Decision made today. Vitals today 116 over 75, pulse 79. Short of breath carrying groceries up one flight, fine on the flat, no orthopnea now. Class II to III. 92 days on full guideline-directed therapy at target doses, tolerating, potassium 4.4, blood pressure 102 over 63.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.

Repeat transthoracic echocardiogram after 3 months of optimized medical therapy. Left ventricular ejection fraction 28 percent by biplane Simpson’s, unchanged. Persistent anterior and apical akinesis.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 233, LDL 126, HDL 50, triglycerides 171. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Pre-procedure visit for device implant. Hold the apixaban one dose, continue the rest. Chest X-ray and labs fine. Consent signed.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
